target.title: fix: make `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` install never fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Solves issues where installing `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` might fail if the current system is incompatible with the available `node-llama-cpp` prebuilt binaries and building the native bindings from source also fails.

[Setting `config.nodeLlamaCppPostinstall` to `"ignoreFailedBuild"`](https://node-llama-cpp.withcat.ai/guide/troubleshooting#postinstall-behavior) allows the package installation to complete in that rare case, while still allowing `node-llama-cpp` to try building from source later when it is first used.

## Why This Change Was Made

This updates the llama.cpp provider to `node-llama-cpp` v3.19 and configures its postinstall behavior to avoid blocking provider installation when the native fallback build cannot complete. The change keeps the normal install path unchanged for compatible systems, and only changes the failure behavior for uncommon environments where neither a prebuilt binary nor a build from source is available.

This also brings the provider onto the latest `node-llama-cpp` release, including upstream improvements such as optimized arm prebuilt binaries.

## User Impact

Users are less likely to have OpenClaw extension installation fail because of a native `node-llama-cpp` build issue on their machine.

On systems where the prebuilt binaries are compatible, users should see no behavioral change. On systems where installation previously failed during `node-llama-cpp` postinstall, installation can now complete, and any remaining native build issue is deferred until the llama.cpp provider is actually used.

## Evidence

* Updated `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` to depend on `node-llama-cpp` `^3.19.0`.
* Added `config.nodeLlamaCppPostinstall: "ignoreFailedBuild"` to the provider package metadata.
* Regenerated the package lock/shrinkwrap files for the dependency update.
* The `node-llama-cpp` docs describe `ignoreFailedBuild` as preserving the default postinstall behavior, except that a failed fallback source build is ignored so installation can still succeed.
* I did not reproduce the rare incompatible-prebuilt plus failed-source-build environment locally; this change relies on the documented upstream postinstall behavior.
